transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, and um, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I guess I came in because... well, I've just been having a little bit of trouble keeping things organized lately. It's not a huge disaster or anything! I just feel like I can't get my schoolwork and my little accessories shop organized at the same time. I try really hard to keep on top of it, but my shop supplies, my receipts, and then my assignment notes and due dates... they all sort of just end up in these big piles. And then I look at it all and I just don't know what to do first. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's an okay reason to be here.
Has this difficulty with organizing your tasks been a struggle for you throughout most of your life, or is this something that has only started happening recently?

Well, I guess... I mean, I've always been a little bit scattered, maybe? But it hasn't always been this bad. I'd say it really became a, um, a noticeable issue about two years and two months ago. 

That was when I changed schools. I started this business program, which is great, but there's just so much less structure than I was used to in high school. And trying to balance all those new classes with running my accessories shop... it just got a little overwhelming. I really do try my best to keep everything straight, I promise. It's just... a lot to juggle all at once. Does that sound like a normal thing to struggle with when you change schools?
Aside from feeling overwhelmed by your workload, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or uninterested in things you usually enjoy over these past two years?

Oh, um, no! No, definitely not. I hope I didn't make it sound like I'm miserable or anything like that. I'm actually a pretty upbeat person, usually! 

I still really, really love working on my shop and making things, and I like my classes a lot when I'm actually in them. I haven't been feeling sad or down at all... just, you know, a bit frustrated with myself for not keeping up with the piles. 

Is it okay that I'm just disorganized, but not sad? I mean, I hope I'm not wasting your time if I'm just a little messy... I just really want to do a good job with everything.

Looking back at your childhood or early teen years, before you started this program, did you frequently have trouble with things like losing your belongings, forgetting appointments, or being easily distracted?

Well, I guess... um, as a kid, I wasn't really losing things or forgetting things too much. I was actually pretty good at keeping track of my stuff! But, well... I was definitely a little bit, um, energetic? 

My mom actually still has these old notes from my elementary school teachers. They always said I was a really enthusiastic student! But... they also mentioned I had a hard time staying in my seat, and I would sometimes, you know, talk before it was my turn, or kind of rush through group activities. I really did understand the work, I just... I guess I was just eager to get to the next thing? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid. I really tried to be good! Is it normal for kids to just have a little too much energy like that?
Do you find that you have these same struggles with focus and organization when you are working in your shop, or is this difficulty primarily limited to when you are studying for your classes?

Um, I don't think so? I haven't really noticed those same problems when I'm working on my shop. I guess because I'm making things with my hands and moving around, it feels a lot easier to just... get it done, you know? I don't really have to sit still and focus the same way I do for my classes. 

My work table might get a tiny bit cluttered with materials sometimes, but I always get my orders shipped out on time! I promise I don't let my customers down. Is it normal that I can handle the shop okay, but the schoolwork is just... harder for me to keep straight? I hope that makes sense.
Outside of your schoolwork, do you find that you have similar trouble staying focused or keeping track of your responsibilities in your social life or at home?

Um, no, not really! I try really hard to be a good friend and roommate. I mean, my side of the room might get a little bit messy sometimes, but I always make sure to clean it up before it bothers anyone! And I love hanging out with my friends. Sometimes I might talk a little fast or get super excited about what we're doing, but I don't forget when we're supposed to meet up or anything like that. 

I really try to keep my personal life nice and tidy. I hope it doesn't seem like my whole life is a mess just because school is a bit tricky right now. Is it okay that I'm doing alright with my friends and at home?
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior, such as acting out, getting into conflicts, or perhaps withdrawing from your usual social activities, since you started this new program?

Oh, no, definitely not! Um, I really try my best to get along with everybody. I haven't been arguing with anyone or, you know, acting out at all. I promise I'm not a troublemaker! 

And I'm definitely still seeing my friends and doing all my normal stuff, so I haven't pulled away or hidden in my room or anything like that. I really try to stay positive and keep things peaceful with the people around me. 

Um, I hope I don't seem like the kind of person who would cause conflicts? I just want everyone to be happy, really. I'm doing okay with all that, right?
Looking at your current life outside of your shop, do you still find that you frequently talk out of turn, interrupt others, or feel like you have to rush through activities?

Um, well... I really try not to be rude, I promise! I don't want to be someone who interrupts people. But... I guess sometimes in group critiques or, like, class discussions, I might accidentally jump in a little early? 

It's just that I get so excited, and I think I know what the other person is going to say, so I just sort of... blurt out my answer before they're totally finished talking. And then I always feel really embarrassed right after, because I realize I just guessed what they were trying to say and cut them off. I always apologize right away, though! I really don't mean to be disrespectful. Is it okay that I just get a little too eager sometimes? I'm trying to be better about waiting my turn, I really am.
When you are faced with a task that you find boring or uninteresting, do you find it difficult to stay focused and complete it without getting distracted by other things?

Um, well, I really do try my best to pay attention, especially for my business assignments. I know they're super important. But, um... I guess if it's a really long lecture or a video that isn't super exciting, it can be a little bit tough? 

Like, I'll start out listening really closely, but then after a few minutes, my brain just sort of... wanders off? I'll start thinking about, like, new charm designs I want to make, or ideas for packaging orders, which is still related to my work, you know? But then I'll suddenly realize I haven't been listening and I missed half of what the video said. 

I always rewind it and try again, though! I really want to do a good job. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad student just because my mind drifts to my creative projects sometimes. That's pretty normal, right?
Outside of your school environment, do you feel like you have a hard time staying seated or that you feel a constant inner sense of restlessness, even when you are just relaxing at home?

Um, well, I definitely try to relax when I'm at home! I love just hanging out. But... I guess sometimes it's a little tricky for me to just stay completely still? 

Like, if I'm supposed to be sitting and listening to someone, or just watching a movie, I kind of get this... buzzing feeling inside? It's not bad, I promise! It's just like my body feels like it has all this extra energy and I need to be doing something or moving a little bit, even if I'm not actually going anywhere. 

I really try not to bother anyone with it, though! I'll just, you know, wiggle my toes or shift around on the couch so I'm not being disruptive. I hope that doesn't sound too weird? I think a lot of people probably get a little fidgety when they're trying to sit quietly, don't you think?

Aside from your schoolwork, do you find that this 'buzzing' feeling or the tendency to lose focus happens in other settings, like when you are visiting family or in other structured environments outside of school and your shop?

Oh, um... no, I don't really think so? I always try to be on my very best behavior when I'm visiting my family or going to, like, formal things. I'd never want to be disrespectful to my relatives by spacing out while they're talking to me or bouncing around the room! 

So, no, I haven't really noticed that buzzing feeling or losing my focus in those situations. I think I do a pretty good job of just sitting nicely and paying attention when I'm in those kinds of places. It's really mostly just with my school videos or when I'm relaxing on the couch at home, like I mentioned. 

That's a good thing, right? Like, it shows I can hold it together and be polite when it really counts?
When you are with your close friends, do you ever feel that same 'buzzing' energy or find yourself losing focus during your conversations with them?

Um, with my friends? Oh, no, I don't think so. I really value my friends, so I always make sure I'm being a good listener when we hang out. 

I mean, I guess sometimes we get really excited talking about things, and maybe I'll talk a little fast or we'll jump from topic to topic, but that's just because we're having fun, you know? It's not like I'm zoning out on them or anything like that. I would feel terrible if I made them feel like I wasn't paying attention to what they were saying. 

So, yeah, I'm pretty sure I'm totally focused when I'm with them. That's pretty normal for friends to just be energetic together, right? I'm sure it doesn't mean anything bad.
Do you feel that these challenges with organization and focus are causing you genuine distress or significantly interfering with your ability to succeed in your classes or run your shop?

Um... well, I really try not to let it get to me too much! I always try to stay positive, you know? But... I guess it has been a little bit stressful lately. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything! 

But... I kind of missed a few required steps for my school program recently. It was just a silly mistake, really, just getting things mixed up. But now my financial aid is a little bit at risk, which is... not great. I'm sure I can fix it, though! I just need to try harder to be organized. 

And, um, with my shop... the people I usually work with on projects, they've sort of started depending on me a little less? Like, they're giving me fewer tasks to handle. I think they just want to make sure things get done on time, which is totally fair! I don't blame them at all. But it does make me feel a little bad, like I'm letting them down. 

I'm really trying to get better at managing everything, I promise! Do you think things like this happen to a lot of people when they're just trying to juggle school and hobbies? It's just a normal bump in the road, right?

When you are in a situation where you have to wait in a long line or sit through a mandatory meeting where you are not actively engaged, do you find it just as difficult to remain still and focused as you do during your school lectures?

Um, well... waiting in lines is definitely not my favorite thing. I mean, nobody likes waiting, right? 

But, um, I guess I do get a little... fidgety? Like, if I'm standing in line at the financial aid office, or waiting to ask a professor a question after class, I just... I kind of shift my weight a lot, or bounce on my heels. I try really hard not to be annoying about it! I know everyone else is waiting too. 

And, um, sometimes in my art critiques, when we have to go around the room and wait our turn to speak... I get so eager to share my thoughts that I might, um, accidentally jump in a little early? Like, I'll cut in before someone is totally finished. I always apologize right away, though! I never mean to be rude or talk over anyone. It's just that I get so excited about the discussion, you know? 

That's just a sign that I'm really passionate and engaged with the class, right? I'm sure teachers appreciate students who are enthusiastic, even if they're a tiny bit impatient sometimes.

When you are working on your shop or doing things you really enjoy, do you find that you still have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes, even if you feel perfectly calm and not restless at all?

Um... working on my shop? Oh, I love my shop! That's when I'm happiest, really. I make all these little custom resin charms and keychains, and it's just so much fun. 

But, um... mistakes? I mean, I guess everyone makes a little mistake here and there, right? Like, sometimes I might accidentally mix the wrong color tint, or... or I'll forget to put the little metal clasp in before the resin cures. But that's just because I get so wrapped up in the creative process! It's not like I'm not paying attention, I'm just... focusing on the big picture of the design. 

And, you know, a lot of times those "mistakes" actually turn out to be really cool happy accidents! I just list them as one-of-a-kind oopsie items, and people seem to like them okay. So it's really not a big deal at all. 

I'm sure lots of artists have little slip-ups when they're in the zone, don't you think? It just means I have an active, creative mind, right?

target_item.manifestation: In group critiques or class discussions, I jump in with my answer before the other person is done talking, and then I feel embarrassed because I realize I guessed what they were going to say.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question asks if the patient frequently talks out of turn, interrupts others, or feels like they have to rush through activities, which directly relates to the symptom of blurting out answers before a question has been completed.

patient.answer:
Um, well... I really try not to be rude, I promise! I don't want to be someone who interrupts people. But... I guess sometimes in group critiques or, like, class discussions, I might accidentally jump in a little early? 

It's just that I get so excited, and I think I know what the other person is going to say, so I just sort of... blurt out my answer before they're totally finished talking. And then I always feel really embarrassed right after, because I realize I just guessed what they were trying to say and cut them off. I always apologize right away, though! I really don't mean to be disrespectful. Is it okay that I just get a little too eager sometimes? I'm trying to be better about waiting my turn, I really am.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has significant struggles with staying on task or finishing projects when they are not physically engaged or interested in the activity.
doctor.question: When you are faced with a task that you find boring or uninteresting, do you find it difficult to stay focused and complete it without getting distracted by other things?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: In class or when I'm watching a video for my business assignments, I can start out listening, but after a few minutes my mind is on charm designs or order ideas and I realize I missed half of what was said.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about difficulty staying focused on tasks and getting distracted, which directly corresponds to the symptom of Sustained Attention Difficulty.

patient.answer:
Um, well, I really do try my best to pay attention, especially for my business assignments. I know they're super important. But, um... I guess if it's a really long lecture or a video that isn't super exciting, it can be a little bit tough? 

Like, I'll start out listening really closely, but then after a few minutes, my brain just sort of... wanders off? I'll start thinking about, like, new charm designs I want to make, or ideas for packaging orders, which is still related to my work, you know? But then I'll suddenly realize I haven't been listening and I missed half of what the video said. 

I always rewind it and try again, though! I really want to do a good job. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad student just because my mind drifts to my creative projects sometimes. That's pretty normal, right?

inference.note: Ruled out F90.1 (Predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation) because the patient reports significant difficulties with organization and focus (inattentive symptoms) in addition to impulsivity, and the symptoms are not solely or primarily hyperactive-impulsive.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient currently meets the formal diagnostic criteria for hyperactivity/impulsivity in multiple settings (home/social) vs. just in school/structured settings to differentiate between ADHD subtypes.
doctor.question: Outside of your school environment, do you feel like you have a hard time staying seated or that you feel a constant inner sense of restlessness, even when you are just relaxing at home?

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: Even when I'm not actually going anywhere, I feel like my body is buzzing and I need to be moving, especially when I'm supposed to sit still and listen.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling a constant inner sense of restlessness, which directly corresponds to symptom S012 (Feeling_Restless).

patient.answer:
Um, well, I definitely try to relax when I'm at home! I love just hanging out. But... I guess sometimes it's a little tricky for me to just stay completely still? 

Like, if I'm supposed to be sitting and listening to someone, or just watching a movie, I kind of get this... buzzing feeling inside? It's not bad, I promise! It's just like my body feels like it has all this extra energy and I need to be doing something or moving a little bit, even if I'm not actually going anywhere. 

I really try not to bother anyone with it, though! I'll just, you know, wiggle my toes or shift around on the couch so I'm not being disruptive. I hope that doesn't sound too weird? I think a lot of people probably get a little fidgety when they're trying to sit quietly, don't you think?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity are present in two or more settings, which is a diagnostic criterion for ADHD.
doctor.question: Aside from your schoolwork, do you find that this 'buzzing' feeling or the tendency to lose focus happens in other settings, like when you are visiting family or in other structured environments outside of school and your shop?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the presence of symptoms in multiple settings (pervasiveness), which is not explicitly covered by a specific symptom profile item in the provided list. The patient's profile has duration, functional impairment, and onset, but not a specific 'multiple settings' criterion item to select.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... no, I don't really think so? I always try to be on my very best behavior when I'm visiting my family or going to, like, formal things. I'd never want to be disrespectful to my relatives by spacing out while they're talking to me or bouncing around the room! 

So, no, I haven't really noticed that buzzing feeling or losing my focus in those situations. I think I do a pretty good job of just sitting nicely and paying attention when I'm in those kinds of places. It's really mostly just with my school videos or when I'm relaxing on the couch at home, like I mentioned. 

That's a good thing, right? Like, it shows I can hold it together and be polite when it really counts?

inference.note: The patient's symptoms are highly context-dependent and appear largely limited to academic or low-stimulation environments, with significant ability to compensate in other areas. This suggests the symptoms may not meet the full diagnostic criteria for pervasive ADHD (F90.x), prompting the inclusion of a code for other symptoms involving restricted attention/behavior.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are pervasive enough across multiple settings to meet the diagnostic criteria for ADHD, or if they are context-dependent.
doctor.question: When you are with your close friends, do you ever feel that same 'buzzing' energy or find yourself losing focus during your conversations with them?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient experiences the 'buzzing' energy (restlessness) or loses focus (sustained attention difficulty) when with close friends, which is inquiring about the presence of symptoms in a third setting (friends) to establish cross-situationality. The symptom profile does not provide specific information about how the patient acts with close friends regarding these symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um, with my friends? Oh, no, I don't think so. I really value my friends, so I always make sure I'm being a good listener when we hang out. 

I mean, I guess sometimes we get really excited talking about things, and maybe I'll talk a little fast or we'll jump from topic to topic, but that's just because we're having fun, you know? It's not like I'm zoning out on them or anything like that. I would feel terrible if I made them feel like I wasn't paying attention to what they were saying. 

So, yeah, I'm pretty sure I'm totally focused when I'm with them. That's pretty normal for friends to just be energetic together, right? I'm sure it doesn't mean anything bad.

inference.note: The patient's symptoms are highly situational (primarily academic), which is inconsistent with a pervasive diagnosis of ADHD (F90.x). The lack of impairment in other domains (social, work, home) suggests these symptoms may not reach the threshold for a clinical disorder, making R46.89 (Other symptoms and signs involving appearance and behavior) a more appropriate consideration than a formal ADHD diagnosis.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms cause clinically significant impairment in social, academic, or occupational functioning, which is a core diagnostic criterion for ADHD.
doctor.question: Do you feel that these challenges with organization and focus are causing you genuine distress or significantly interfering with your ability to succeed in your classes or run your shop?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: Because of all this, I missed required steps for my program and my financial aid is now at risk, and people I work with on shop projects have started depending on me less.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the symptoms are causing genuine distress or significantly interfering with the patient's ability to succeed in classes or run the shop, which directly assesses functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Um... well, I really try not to let it get to me too much! I always try to stay positive, you know? But... I guess it has been a little bit stressful lately. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything! 

But... I kind of missed a few required steps for my school program recently. It was just a silly mistake, really, just getting things mixed up. But now my financial aid is a little bit at risk, which is... not great. I'm sure I can fix it, though! I just need to try harder to be organized. 

And, um, with my shop... the people I usually work with on projects, they've sort of started depending on me a little less? Like, they're giving me fewer tasks to handle. I think they just want to make sure things get done on time, which is totally fair! I don't blame them at all. But it does make me feel a little bad, like I'm letting them down. 

I'm really trying to get better at managing everything, I promise! Do you think things like this happen to a lot of people when they're just trying to juggle school and hobbies? It's just a normal bump in the road, right?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are pervasive across multiple settings or restricted to specific environments to distinguish between ADHD presentations.
doctor.question: When you are in a situation where you have to wait in a long line or sit through a mandatory meeting where you are not actively engaged, do you find it just as difficult to remain still and focused as you do during your school lectures?

target_item.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: Waiting for my turn to speak in critiques, stand in financial aid lines, or ask a question after class makes me so impatient that I keep shifting around and sometimes cut in before I mean to.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about situations where the patient has to wait in a long line or sit through a mandatory meeting where they are not actively engaged, which directly maps to the symptom of having difficulty waiting one's turn (S017).

patient.answer:
Um, well... waiting in lines is definitely not my favorite thing. I mean, nobody likes waiting, right? 

But, um, I guess I do get a little... fidgety? Like, if I'm standing in line at the financial aid office, or waiting to ask a professor a question after class, I just... I kind of shift my weight a lot, or bounce on my heels. I try really hard not to be annoying about it! I know everyone else is waiting too. 

And, um, sometimes in my art critiques, when we have to go around the room and wait our turn to speak... I get so eager to share my thoughts that I might, um, accidentally jump in a little early? Like, I'll cut in before someone is totally finished. I always apologize right away, though! I never mean to be rude or talk over anyone. It's just that I get so excited about the discussion, you know? 

That's just a sign that I'm really passionate and engaged with the class, right? I'm sure teachers appreciate students who are enthusiastic, even if they're a tiny bit impatient sometimes.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient meets the full diagnostic criteria for ADHD (inattentive type vs. hyperactive-impulsive type vs. combined type) by asking if the symptoms of inattention are present independently of the hyperactive symptoms.
doctor.question: When you are working on your shop or doing things you really enjoy, do you find that you still have trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes, even if you feel perfectly calm and not restless at all?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about failing to give close attention to details or making careless mistakes, which corresponds to symptom S001. This is not in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Um... working on my shop? Oh, I love my shop! That's when I'm happiest, really. I make all these little custom resin charms and keychains, and it's just so much fun. 

But, um... mistakes? I mean, I guess everyone makes a little mistake here and there, right? Like, sometimes I might accidentally mix the wrong color tint, or... or I'll forget to put the little metal clasp in before the resin cures. But that's just because I get so wrapped up in the creative process! It's not like I'm not paying attention, I'm just... focusing on the big picture of the design. 

And, you know, a lot of times those "mistakes" actually turn out to be really cool happy accidents! I just list them as one-of-a-kind oopsie items, and people seem to like them okay. So it's really not a big deal at all. 

I'm sure lots of artists have little slip-ups when they're in the zone, don't you think? It just means I have an active, creative mind, right?

inference.note: The patient's symptoms (persistent difficulty with organization and focus, restlessness, and impulsivity dating back to childhood, now causing significant impairment in academic and professional life) are consistent with ADHD, Predominantly Inattentive/Hyperactive-Impulsive Presentation. Given the clear evidence of both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms that interfere with functioning, F90.0 is the most appropriate diagnosis.
